content: Dont worry about tie-breaking cases. The test cases were specifically picked so target values never hit exact halfway points like .xx5. Because of that, default 2-decimal float formatting in any language (whether it uses Python's Banker's rounding, C++, Java, etc.) will give the exact same output and standard print formatting will pass everything

✅ Approved the contribution.
Comment: It is an engaging problem that will make people think without being too difficult and hard to understand.

Good puzzle and good progression in the tests, well done! A few corrections needed before I can approve personally:

- What rounding algorithm? If multiple work, please provide them, to ensure cross-language compatibility.
- Some tests and validators are unnamed.

Formatting
* Please study the formatting syntax described on this page: https://www.codingame.com/playgrounds/40701/help-center/statement , and format your statement properly as described in the points below.

Goal
* Please format N as a [[variable]].

* Please format 0, 100 and 0.4 as {{constants}}.

* Please format all keywords in <<bold>>.

Input
* Please format N and X as [[variables]].

* Please format "Line 1" and "Next [[N]] lines" in <<bold>>.

Output
* Please format "Line 1" and "Line 2" in <<bold>>.

* Line 1: Please remove the example.

* Line 1: Please specify whether to *round* or *truncate* Target Value to 2 decimal places.

Constraints
* Please format N and X as [[variables]].

Input/Cases
* If the chosen numbers are always in ascending order, please specify that in the input description. Otherwise, please randomise the order of the chosen numbers in some of the cases.

Cases
* Please remove all trailing newlines from:
  • the input for all cases except Test 1.
  • the output for all cases.

* Each test and its validator should cover the *same scenario* with slightly different inputs and slightly different outputs (if applicable). Please split the current 4 pairs of cases into 8 accordingly.

Thanks.
Done! That was really helpful!
Hey, thanks for the feedback! Well,I've updated it! Lemme know if there're any corrections that need to be done to get it approved!
Yes, this is a problem that will make people think what rounding rule is actually required, when the output description mentions three different rules: half-up, half-even, half-down 🤔

Thank you for your clarification.

Listing "half-up, half-even or half-down" in the Output section could imply that players need to choose or implement a specific rounding rule.

You could instead state in the Constraints section that the test cases are specifically chosen so that the Target Value never falls exactly halfway between two 2-decimal values, so half-up, half-even and half-down rounding will produce the same result.
Good point! Well, I've updated the statement to keep the Output section clean and moved that note over to the Constraints section so players don't get confused. Thanks for the suggestion!
Thanks for the review and approval! Glad you liked the puzzle setup.
Yeah, fair point! That’s exactly why the test suite avoids .xx5 halfway ties completely so people don't have to stress about language-specific float quirks!

Here's the thing, Python doesn't do half-up rounding, it actually does half-even rounding (or "banker's rounding"), meaning it rounds to the nearest even:

>>> "%.02f" % .745
'0.74'
>>> "%.02f" % .755
'0.76'

As long as you ensure that you don't have a .xx5 target value case in your examples, you should be able to just specify the following, which should be enough for a CoC:

> rounded to exactly 2 decimal places (half-up, half-even or half-down rounding).

Sorry for this, floating point / decimal rounding modes are often misunderstood and as soon as a puzzle makes use of them, especially on a platform like CodinGame which supports many programming languages, it can quickly be unfair :)
I've updated the statement rounding description to include half-up, half-even, or half-down rounding, and renamed all 24 test cases and validators. Thanks again for the review!

Output
* "Line 1: The calculated Target Value, rounded to exactly 2 decimal places(half-up, half-even or half-down rounding)."

Which rounding rule is required? Half-up, half-even or half-down? They are three different rules! https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/integration-bus/10.0.0?topic=functions-round-function

No problem 🙂

The cases still need a bit more work:

* Validator 8: Please remove the trailing newline from the output.

* It's good that each case pair now covers the same scenario. However, the expected outputs should also differ slightly whenever possible, rather than every test expecting exactly the same output as its corresponding validator.

* In most of the visible tests, the chosen numbers are in ascending order. Please revise at least half of them so that the numbers appear in a random order.

* In the previous version there are cases with large player pool (i.e. N ≥ 10). Please:

  • add a case pair with N between 21 and 30.

  • add a case pair with N between 41 and 50.

* Please also make sure the chosen numbers are generated randomly in the new cases.

Thanks.

Done! Different test cases define the actual difficulty level rising with each test case.

Thanks!

Cases
* The cases listed below look good, but please consider renaming them, as their current names don't reflect what the cases are testing (e.g. not tie breakers, not sorted):
  • Absolute Tie-Breaker (Equidistant Matches) (Test 4)
  • Dual Value Tie-Breaker (Test 5)
  • High Number Clustering (Sorted) (Test 6)
  • Low Decimals Precision Rounding (Sorted) (Test 7)
  • Floating Point Halfway Tie (Sorted) (Test 8)

* Could you also add two pairs of genuine tie-breaker cases: one pair with N < 10 and another with N > 25?

Thanks.
